services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/AdminPermissions.java:77 — With V2 enabled, the ClientRemovedEvent cleanup is skipped and nothing deletes the V2 per-client resource, so permissions stay bound to the deleted client's id and silently apply again if a client with the same id is re-imported.

goldens.comment: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.

In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope)`, if no per-client `Resource` exists (`resourceStore.findByName(server, client.getId(), ...)` returns null), the code explicitly falls back to evaluating permissions against the resource-type (“all-clients”) resource via `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(..., CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)` and then evaluates all its scopes. There is no exclusion for special/internal clients (e.g., realm-management or the admin-permissions client), so an all-clients grant for `MAP_ROLES` / `MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE` would apply to those clients as well. The finding’s broader “take over the realm” claim depends on other code not shown, but the overly-broad fallback behavior itself is directly present in the diff and is security-relevant.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `resolveClient(KeycloakSession session, String id)` that resolves first via `getClientById(realm, id)` and only then `getClientByClientId(realm, id)`. If callers pass a clientId string, and that string happens to equal some other client's internal ID, the lookup will resolve to the wrong client. However, the finding's phrasing about a "custom internal id" is not supported by the diff, and the API appears to generally use internal IDs for resources (e.g., tests create permissions with `myclient.getId()`), so this is more of an ambiguity/edge-case concern than a clearly verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication.rationale: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the code first looks up a per-client Resource by name (client.getId()). It only falls back to evaluating the "all-clients" resource type (AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) when that per-client resource is null. If a per-client resource exists for any reason (e.g., created due to a permission for another user/admin or for a different scope), and the caller relies on an all-clients grant, the method will evaluate only the per-client resource and will not consider the all-clients permission—contradicting the interface/javadoc claims that permissions like MANAGE/VIEW for "all clients" should apply. This behavior is directly shown by the resource == null conditional fallback.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `ClientPermissionsV2` implementation, multiple previously-supported `ClientPermissions` operations are overridden to unconditionally throw `UnsupportedOperationException` (e.g., `canExchangeTo`, `isPermissionsEnabled`, `setPermissionsEnabled`, `resource`, `getPermissions`, and several `*Permission(...)` methods). The diff does not show any guarding/disabling of the corresponding endpoints/uses, so this introduces a concrete risk of 500s when those methods are invoked under V2.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds CLIENTS support in AdminPermissionsSchema: a new CLIENTS resource type and scopes, adds it to the schema map, and adds a CLIENTS branch in getOrCreateResource() to resolve the resource name via resolveClient(session, id). Therefore the claim that there is "no CLIENTS branch" causing null display names is contradicted by the shown changes. The referenced getResourceName method/line 310 is not present in the diff, so the specific assertion about that method cannot be verified here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/PermissionClientTest.java:326 — The new MAP_ROLES tests only check the positive case and never assert that single-client or all-clients MAP_ROLES is denied for another client's or realm-management's roles, so the escalation paths above would still pass.

adjudication.rationale: In PermissionClientTest, the new test `testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient()` only asserts (a) operations are forbidden before granting permissions, then (b) operations succeed after granting `MAP_ROLES` on the user plus `MAP_ROLES`/`MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE`/`CONFIGURE` on the specific client (`createPermission(... myclient.getId(), clientsType, Set.of(MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, CONFIGURE), ...)`). It does not add a follow-up assertion that mapping roles/composites remains forbidden for a different client (or another sensitive client like realm-management) after those permissions are granted. That is a concrete, diff-grounded test coverage gap for the newly added client-scoped MAP_ROLES logic, not a verifiable functional defect in production code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:188 — ClientPermissionsV2 overrides ClientPermissionEvaluator isPermissionsEnabled/setPermissionsEnabled/getPermissions to throw UnsupportedOperationException, so the existing admin REST GET/PUT /clients/{id}/management/permissions endpoints (which previously got the V1 impl under MgmtPermissionsV2) now fail with HTTP 500 under FGAP V2, and the interface Javadoc does not document it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff wires FGAP V2 client permission evaluation to `ClientPermissionsV2` by overriding `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` to return a `ClientPermissionsV2` instance. In `ClientPermissionsV2`, several previously-available operations (`isPermissionsEnabled`, `setPermissionsEnabled`, `getPermissions`, and others like `resource(...)`) are overridden to unconditionally throw `UnsupportedOperationException`. Any existing code path that calls these methods via `management(...).clients()` will now fail at runtime (likely surfacing as 500s if invoked from REST). The diff itself shows the behavioral change (new override + UOE throws), even though the specific REST endpoint call sites are not in this patch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:148 — canExchangeTo now throws UnsupportedOperationException under FGAP V2 (it used to fall through to the V1 ClientPermissions), so legacy client-to-client token exchange at the public token endpoint returns 500 instead of an allow/deny, and the CLIENTS schema has no token-exchange scope to replace it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that in `ClientPermissionsV2` several client permission operations are explicitly made unsupported by throwing `UnsupportedOperationException`, including `canExchangeTo(...)` (and `exchangeToPermission(...)`) with message "Not supported in V2". It also shows the new `AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS` scopes list does not include any token-exchange-related scope (only CONFIGURE/MANAGE/VIEW/MAP_ROLES variants). However, the claim that this necessarily causes the public token endpoint legacy client-to-client token exchange to return HTTP 500 cannot be verified from this PR diff alone (no call sites / token endpoint wiring shown). The actionable, diff-grounded issue is that V2 introduces a `clients()` permission evaluator that may be selected by `MgmtPermissionsV2`, while token-exchange-related methods in the V2 evaluator are unimplemented and would throw if invoked.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:87 — In V2, canView() (and so canViewClientScopes/canListClientScopes/requireView) accepts only the VIEW permission, while canManage(), canManageClientScopes() and canView(ClientScopeModel) accept all-clients MANAGE; this breaks the V1 rule that manage implies view, so a MANAGE-all-clients admin can manage client scopes but gets 403 listing them.

adjudication.rationale: In ClientPermissionsV2, global `canView()` is implemented as `return canViewClientDefault() || hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW);` and does not consider `MANAGE` (unlike V1’s typical “manage implies view” behavior). Meanwhile global `canManage()` and `canManageClientScopes()` both accept the all-clients `MANAGE` permission (`hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`). This creates an inconsistency where an admin granted only all-clients `MANAGE` (but not `VIEW`) can satisfy manage checks but fail view/list checks that rely on `canView()` (e.g., `canListClientScopes()` per the interface docs depends on `canView()`), leading to 403s for listing/viewing while still being allowed to manage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionEvaluator.java:96 — The new Javadoc on the void methods requireView() (line 96) and requireViewClientScopes() (line 101) says they "Return true", but they actually throw ForbiddenException, so the documented contract is wrong.

adjudication.rationale: In ClientPermissionEvaluator, the new Javadoc for the void methods `requireView()` and `requireViewClientScopes()` incorrectly says "Returns {@code true}" even though the methods return `void` and are intended to throw `ForbiddenException` when the corresponding `can*()` check is false. This is a concrete, diff-introduced documentation/contract mismatch, but it does not demonstrate a runtime behavior defect in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:219 — getResourceTypeResource() can return null (realm adminPermissionsEnabled=false while admin-permissions client exists, or realm initialized before "Clients" type existed) and findByResource(server, null) is called without a null check, so every canManage/canView(client) for non-role admins can NPE instead of returning false.
matched_golden_ids: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate points to the same underlying bug: getResourceTypeResource() may return null in ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, and the code calls findByResource with that null value, leading to a potential NullPointerException. It also recommends/implies the need for a null check/defensive handling, aligning with the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:214 — Once any per-client resource exists, evaluation uses only that untyped resource (created without setType in AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource), so all-clients permissions bound to the "Clients" resource are skipped for that client, contradicting the Javadoc "also if permission to X all clients".

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope)`, the code first resolves a per-client `Resource` via `resourceStore.findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId())`. It only falls back to evaluating the all-clients resource (`AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(... CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)`) when the per-client resource is `null`. If a per-client resource exists but does not grant the requested scope (or has no policies), the method never evaluates the all-clients permission, so a granted all-clients permission can be incorrectly ignored for that client—contradicting the Javadoc claims like “also if ... permission ... all clients.” The finding’s mention about the resource being created “without setType” is not verifiable from the shown diff, but the all-clients-skipped behavior is.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:138 — getClientsWithPermission uses findByType("Clients"), but per-client resources are created with no type, so it never returns specific client IDs and instead returns the sentinel resource name "Clients" when an all-clients permission is granted.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly introduces a client ResourceType in AdminPermissionsSchema (`CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE = "Clients"` and `CLIENTS = new ResourceType(...)`) and registers it in the schema map (`super(Map.of(..., CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, CLIENTS))`). Resource creation for the client type is also wired via `getOrCreateResource(... )` with `resolveClient(...)` to produce the per-client resource name. Nothing in the diff shows per-client client resources being created "with no type"; on the contrary, they are associated with the `Clients` resource type, so `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` is not verifiably broken for per-client resources based on this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:87 — canView() only checks the all-clients VIEW scope, not MANAGE, so an admin with an all-clients MANAGE permission gets canManageClientScopes()=true but canViewClientScopes()/canListClientScopes()=false and cannot list the client scopes they can manage (V1's MANAGE_CLIENTS role does imply view).

adjudication.rationale: In the new `ClientPermissionsV2`, global `canView()` is implemented as `return canViewClientDefault() || hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW);` and does not treat all-clients `MANAGE` as implying view (unlike `canView(ClientScopeModel)` which explicitly allows `VIEW` or `MANAGE`). At the same time, `canManageClientScopes()` returns true on all-clients `MANAGE` (`return hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE);`). Given the interface contract/comments that `canViewClientScopes()`/`canListClientScopes()` are based on `canView()`, an admin granted only all-clients `MANAGE` would be able to manage client scopes but fail view/list checks for client scopes because `canView()` remains false. This inconsistency is directly grounded in the diff and can break expected behavior where manage implies view.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java:226 — init() returns early for realms whose admin-permissions client already exists, so those realms never get the new "Clients" resource or the configure/map-roles-client-scope/map-roles-composite scopes, and creating CLIENTS permissions fails ("Scope does not exist"/"No scopes found").

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add the new CLIENTS resource type and new scopes in AdminPermissionsSchema (CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, CONFIGURE, MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE) and includes CLIENTS in the schema map passed to super(). However, the finding hinges on behavior in an init() method at/around line 226 that “returns early” and therefore doesn’t create/update resources/scopes for existing realms. No init() method or early-return logic is shown anywhere in the provided diff, so the alleged failure mode (“Scope does not exist”/“No scopes found” because realms never get the new resource/scopes) is not verifiable from this PR diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/AdminPermissions.java:77 — Gating the removal listener on the v1 flag means cleanup of v1 permissions for deleted roles/clients/groups stops whenever FGAP v1 is disabled (previously it always ran), and with v2 on, per-client "Clients" resources/permissions for deleted clients are left orphaned.
matched_golden_ids: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Yes. The candidate flags the same core bug: the removal/cleanup listener is incorrectly gated by the v1 fine-grained authz flag, so when v2 is enabled but v1 is disabled the cleanup logic doesn’t run and permissions/resources for deleted entities become orphaned. This matches the golden issue about inconsistent flag usage (v1 vs v2) leading to missed cleanup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java:310 — getResourceName has no CLIENTS branch, so client permission resources (named by client UUID, no display name) resolve to resource.getDisplayName(), which is null, instead of the clientId or "All clients".

adjudication.rationale: The finding references a `getResourceName` method and claims it lacks a CLIENTS branch at a specific line (~310), but the provided diff does not show any `getResourceName` implementation or any changes around that area. The diff does show CLIENTS support added in `getOrCreateResource` via `resolveClient(...)`, but it does not provide evidence about how resource names/display names are later resolved. Therefore the claim cannot be verified from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:188 — isPermissionsEnabled/setPermissionsEnabled now throw UnsupportedOperationException under V2, so V1-era callers such as the client management/permissions endpoint return a 500 instead of the previous "disabled" result.

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes `ClientPermissionsV2.isPermissionsEnabled(...)` and `setPermissionsEnabled(...)` unconditionally throw `UnsupportedOperationException` (new file `ClientPermissionsV2.java`). At the same time, `AdminPermissions.registerListener` still calls `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false)` on `ClientRemovedEvent` (and similar calls for roles/groups), now gated behind `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ`. If the V2 management path is active (`MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` now returns `ClientPermissionsV2`), these events will trigger an uncaught `UnsupportedOperationException`, leading to server errors (500) during such operations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:262 — Private getEvaluationContext (copied from V1 token-exchange path) is never called, and it is the only user of the ClientModelIdentity/DefaultEvaluationContext/EvaluationContext imports.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:46 — Unused static import TOKEN_EXCHANGE and unused `logger` field (line 51) are leftover copy-paste noise.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:224 — The evaluate-permission-then-match-scope loop is written three times (hasPermission(ClientModel,String), hasPermission(String) at 249, hasGrantedPermission at 276); the two hasPermission overloads should just resolve a resource and delegate to hasGrantedPermission, and the single-element Arrays.asList(scope) is pointless.

However, this is a refactoring/DRY suggestion and minor efficiency/style nit, not a verifiable correctness/security defect or a substantive diff-created design problem that must be addressed for the PR to work.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:244 — hasPermission(String) looks up the all-clients resource with a raw resourceStore.findByName(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...), but hasPermission(ClientModel,...) at line 217 uses AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource, so the same lookup is done two different ways in one class.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows two different code paths for resolving the “all clients” (resource-type) Resource inside the same class. In hasPermission(ClientModel, String) the fallback uses AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE), while hasPermission(String) directly does resourceStore.findByName(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, server.getId()) and returns false if missing. This inconsistency is real and could lead to different behavior depending on which method is called (e.g., if the resource is created/located differently by the schema helper), but the diff alone doesn’t prove it causes incorrect behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:147 — 12 inherited ClientPermissions/ClientPermissionManagement methods are overridden to throw UnsupportedOperationException, so V2 is a subtype that rejects half its parent API; misuse only shows up at runtime and there is no narrower V2 interface.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `ClientPermissionsV2 extends ClientPermissions` and explicitly overrides a set of inherited API methods to throw `UnsupportedOperationException` (e.g., `canExchangeTo`, `exchangeToPermission`, `mapRolesPermission`, `managePermission`, `configurePermission`, `viewPermission`, `isPermissionsEnabled`, `setPermissionsEnabled`, `resource`, `getPermissions`, etc.). This is verifiable in the new file `ClientPermissionsV2.java` and means callers typed to `ClientPermissions` can compile but fail at runtime if they hit those methods. The diff does not show a narrower V2 interface/type that would prevent misuse at compile time. While this may be an intentional design choice, it is a concrete architecture/API contract concern introduced by the change rather than a proven functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/AdminPermissions.java:77 — The removal listener now only runs when the V1 ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature is on, and that gate is the only thing stopping calls into ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled (which throws). This coupling is not documented, and it leaves the V2 branch of management() unreachable from this listener.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows AdminPermissions.registerListener now wraps all removal handling in `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)` (services/.../AdminPermissions.java). The same diff introduces `ClientPermissionsV2`, where `setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean)` is overridden to throw `UnsupportedOperationException` (services/.../ClientPermissionsV2.java). While the diff does not show how `management(...)` chooses between V1 vs V2, it does demonstrate an implicit coupling: this listener will never execute unless that feature is enabled, and it calls `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(...)`, which would be incompatible with `ClientPermissionsV2` if it were ever returned. The claim that this gate is the *only* thing preventing the call (and that V2 is unreachable) cannot be fully verified from the diff, but the coupling/feature-gating concern is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:118 — canView(ClientScopeModel) repeats the role check inline and evaluates permissions twice (VIEW then MANAGE) when it could reuse canView()/canManageClientScopes(), and both ClientScope overrides ignore their argument.

adjudication.rationale: In ClientPermissionsV2, the ClientScope-specific overrides do ignore their argument: canManage(ClientScopeModel) just delegates to canManageClientScopes(), and canView(ClientScopeModel) does not use the clientScope parameter at all. Also, canView(ClientScopeModel) performs two separate permission evaluations via hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW) || hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE); each hasPermission(...) calls root.evaluatePermission(...), so this duplicates potentially expensive evaluation work. While this is not a clear functional defect from the diff alone (it may be intentional that client-scope access is realm-wide), it is a specific, diff-grounded maintainability/performance concern and could be refactored to reuse/centralize logic or evaluate once and check both scopes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java:53 — The blank line after the class declaration was changed to one with only trailing whitespace, which adds noise to the diff.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows an empty line after the class declaration changed from a truly blank line to a line containing only spaces (`-` empty line to `+    `). This is a purely formatting/trailing-whitespace noise issue and not a functional defect or substantive review concern per the categories.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java:91 — getOrCreateResource picks a resolver through an if/else chain on the resource type, and each type needs a new near-copy resolver (resolveClient at 175 copies resolveUser's lookup by id, then by name); the resolver should live on ResourceType or in a map.

This is not a functional defect, but it does concretely increase duplication and the need to edit this method for each new resource type, supporting the architectural/maintainability concern raised in the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionEvaluator.java:96 — The new Javadoc on the void methods requireView() and requireViewClientScopes() (line 101) says "Returns {@code true}", copied from the can* docs, when these methods actually throw ForbiddenException.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff for `ClientPermissionEvaluator.java`, the newly added Javadoc for `void requireView()` and `void requireViewClientScopes()` incorrectly starts with “Returns {@code true} ...”, even though these methods return `void` and are intended to throw `ForbiddenException` when the corresponding `can*` method is false. This is a real, diff-grounded documentation correctness issue, not a runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/AbstractPermissionTest.java:136 — The new createClientPolicy helper has no callers and repeats the body of createUserPolicy almost exactly.

The implementation of createClientPolicy also largely duplicates createUserPolicy (construct representation, set name/logic, create via admin client, register cleanup), differing mainly in policy type and addClient vs addUser. adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/AbstractPermissionTest.java:54 — Helpers were made static and take an explicit ManagedClient even though the base class already injects `client`, so every call site passes `client` for nothing; the static/instance split is also inconsistent (getPolicies and createPermission(client, resourceId, ...) at 163 are instance methods, createAllPermission is static).

Additionally, helper methods remain instance-based (e.g., `protected PoliciesResource getPolicies()` still uses the instance `client`), while other related helpers are static (`createAllPermission` is static, but `createPermission(ManagedClient, resourceId, ...)` is an instance method even though it takes `client`). adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/PermissionClientTest.java:79 — The @AfterEach step that deletes all scope permissions is now written a third time (also in UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest:71 and UserResourceTypePermissionTest:66) instead of moving into AbstractPermissionTest with the other shared helpers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java:168 — The mechanical refactor left odd id lookups: it builds a representation just to read newUserId back, and line 86 makes a REST call via userAlice.admin().toRepresentation().getId() where other call sites use userAlice.getId().

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show some redundant ID retrieval in UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest (e.g., using userAlice.admin().toRepresentation().getId() in testSingleUserPermission, and later building a UserConfigBuilder only to call .build().getId()). However, these are functionally equivalent to using userAlice.getId() / newUserId and are not a verifiable correctness defect introduced by the PR—at most a minor cleanup/perf nit in test code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:217 — The "all clients" fallback in hasPermission(client) doesn't exclude the realm-management or admin-permissions clients, so an all-clients map-roles or map-roles-composite grant makes canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles return true for realm-management; RolePermissions.canMapRole/canMapComposite return early on that result without checkAdminRoles, which lets the admin assign or compose realm-admin.

adjudication.rationale: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), when no per-client Resource exists it falls back to evaluating the resource-type ("all-clients") resource via AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(..., CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) with no special-casing for sensitive clients like "realm-management" or "admin-permissions". Since canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles simply return hasPermission(client, MAP_ROLES / MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE), an all-clients grant of these scopes would make those methods return true for any client, including realm-management, enabling role-mapping against realm-management client roles (which include admin-like roles) unless other code blocks it (not shown in this diff). The missing exclusion is directly verifiable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java:101 — Client resources are named by the raw client UUID and looked up by name with no type check, so a client created with a chosen internal id (e.g. "Users" or an existing user's UUID) makes a per-client permission attach to that users resource and grant its scopes.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces client resources whose resolved name is the internal client id (UUID) via resolveClient() returning client.getId(). At the same time, permission evaluation in ClientPermissionsV2 looks up a resource only by name (resourceStore.findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId())) without constraining by resource type. Since user resources are also named by id (resolveUser() returns user.getId()), this creates a real type-confusion risk if a resource-name collision exists: a lookup intended for a client could return a non-client resource with the same name, and scopes like "manage"/"view" overlap across types. The finding’s specific example about choosing an internal client id like "Users" isn’t shown to be feasible from the diff, but the underlying defect (no type check + shared name namespace) is grounded in the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:219 — For realms whose admin-permissions client was set up before this change, init() returns early and no "Clients" resource exists, so getResourceTypeResource returns null and findByResource(server, null) fails on every client check by a non-manage-clients admin.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` falls back to `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)` when no per-client resource exists, and then immediately calls `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` without a null-check. If `getResourceTypeResource` can return null (e.g., if the resource-type resource doesn't exist and isn't auto-created), this would break evaluation. However, the finding’s specific claim about an `init()` returning early and older realms lacking the "Clients" resource is not verifiable from the provided diff (no `init()`/bootstrap logic is shown), so the defect scenario cannot be confirmed solely from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java:177 — resolveClient tries the UUID lookup before the clientId lookup, so a client whose clientId equals another client's UUID (e.g. realm-management's) causes a permission meant for it to target the other client.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `resolveClient` which first calls `session.clients().getClientById(realm, id)` and only falls back to `getClientByClientId(realm, id)`. If the caller supplies an identifier that is intended to be a `clientId` but happens to equal some other client's internal UUID, the first lookup will succeed and return the wrong client (`return client.getId()`), causing permissions/resources to be associated with the unintended client. This ambiguity is created by the new lookup order in `resolveClient`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/AdminPermissions.java:77 — With the V2 feature on, the removal listener is now skipped and nothing removes V2 per-client resources or permissions when a client is deleted, so a later client recreated with the same id inherits the stale grants.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the removal listener is now guarded by `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)) { ... }` inside `onEvent`, meaning it runs only when the feature is enabled and is skipped when it is disabled—not “with the V2 feature on” (services/.../AdminPermissions.java). The listener still attempts to handle `ClientRemovedEvent` by calling `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(...)`, so the claim that “nothing removes ... when a client is deleted” due to the listener being skipped is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:101 — The map-roles-client-scope scope (canMapClientScopeRoles) has no test at all; MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE is never referenced in PermissionClientTest.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new scope constant `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` in `AdminPermissionsSchema` and adds `ClientPermissionsV2.canMapClientScopeRoles(ClientModel)` which checks `hasPermission(client, AdminPermissionsSchema.MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE)`. In the updated `PermissionClientTest`, there are static imports for `MAP_ROLES` and `MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE` but not `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE`, and the permissions created in `testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient` use `Set.of(MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, CONFIGURE)`—so `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` is indeed never referenced/tested there. This is a specific missing-test gap for newly added nontrivial authorization logic rather than a proven runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/PermissionClientTest.java:359 — The test grants user MAP_ROLES and client MAP_ROLES+MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE+CONFIGURE in one step, and the pre-grant failures come from the missing user/CONFIGURE permissions, so it would still pass if canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles returned true or checked the wrong scope.

adjudication.rationale: In PermissionClientTest#testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient, the post-grant setup grants both (a) a user permission (USERS resource type, MAP_ROLES) and (b) a client permission (CLIENTS resource type, MAP_ROLES + MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE + CONFIGURE) before re-attempting the two previously-forbidden operations. Because the initial failures could be caused by the missing user-side MAP_ROLES and the success after granting can be explained by the user-side grant alone (and/or by the additionally granted CONFIGURE), the test does not isolate/verify that client-side map-roles/composite checks are correctly tied to MAP_ROLES / MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE specifically. This is a diff-grounded test-coverage/precision issue rather than a functional defect in the implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/PermissionClientTest.java:266 — No client test uses a Logic.NEGATIVE permission, or a per-client permission combined with the all-clients permission (the users tests do this for impersonate), so the deny path in ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission is never exercised.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the newly added client-focused tests in `PermissionClientTest` only create positive permissions (e.g., `createPermission(..., Set.of(MANAGE), ...)`, `createPermission(..., Set.of(CONFIGURE), ...)`, and `createAllPermission(..., Set.of(MANAGE|VIEW), ...)`) and never call the `createPermission(..., Logic logic, ...)` overload with `Logic.NEGATIVE`. There is also no test that combines an all-clients permission (`createAllPermission` for `clientsType`) with a per-client permission to validate precedence/deny behavior. By contrast, the user tests do exercise a negative permission path (e.g., `UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest` creates a NEGATIVE impersonate permission then removes it). Therefore, the deny/edge evaluation paths relevant to `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(...)` are not covered by the added client tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:82 — Per-client VIEW (and MAP_ROLES/CONFIGURE) is never checked to stop a permission on myclient from granting access to realmClient; view is only tested with an all-clients permission, and cross-client isolation is only asserted for MANAGE.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows per-client checks are performed. In `ClientPermissionsV2#hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope)`, it looks up a resource by *that client’s id* (`resourceStore.findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId())`) and only falls back to the all-clients resource type if there are policies attached to that all-clients resource. Therefore, a permission created for `myclient` will not match `realmClient` unless an all-clients permission exists. The finding’s claim that per-client VIEW/MAP_ROLES/CONFIGURE is “never checked” and could grant access cross-client is not supported by the code in the diff (though tests indeed focus more on MANAGE cross-client isolation).

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/PermissionClientTest.java:226 — testConfigureOnlyOneClient regenerates the secret of myclient and invalidates the rotated one, but never restores it, even though realmAdminClient authenticates through myclient. This leaks broken credentials into later tests in the shared realm, depending on test order and token expiry.

adjudication.rationale: In `PermissionClientTest.testConfigureOnlyOneClient`, the test calls `clientResource.generateNewSecret()` and `clientResource.invalidateRotatedSecret()` on the `myclient` client but there is no cleanup/restoration of the original secret afterward (only permissions are deleted in `@AfterEach`). The same class uses `@InjectAdminClient(..., client = "myclient", user = "myadmin")` for `realmAdminClient`, so mutating `myclient` credentials can persist across tests in the shared realm and potentially break later tests depending on token refresh/order.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/PermissionClientTest.java:175 — Tests change shared realm state (myclient name, a default client scope moved to optional, client roles created at 334 and mapped to myadmin) with no cleanup; @AfterEach only deletes permissions.

adjudication.rationale: In PermissionClientTest, several tests mutate shared realm/client state without undoing it. For example, testManageOnlyOneClient updates `myclient` name via `clientResource.update(myclient)` and changes client scope assignments via `removeDefaultClientScope(...)` and `addOptionalClientScope(...)` (around the shown blocks), and testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient creates client roles (`roles().create(role/subRole)`) and then maps/composites them. The class-level `@AfterEach` only removes scope permissions from the admin-permissions client (`permissions.findAll(...).forEach(...remove())`) and does not revert the changed client name, restore default/optional scope configuration, or delete the created roles/role mappings. This is a concrete test isolation/cleanup gap grounded in the diff, likely to cause cross-test interference/flakiness, but it’s not a product defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/PermissionClientTest.java:148 — In the pre-grant check, getDefaultClientScopes() throws Forbidden before removeDefaultClientScope is ever called, so the manage-only removal path is never shown to be forbidden.

adjudication.rationale: In `PermissionClientTest#testManageOnlyOneClient`, the pre-grant negative check for removing a default client scope does `clientResource.getDefaultClientScopes().get(1)` before calling `removeDefaultClientScope(...)`. If `getDefaultClientScopes()` is forbidden (as the test assumes pre-grant), the code will throw before the remove call is reached, so the test does not specifically exercise/verify that `removeDefaultClientScope` itself is forbidden without permissions—only that *some* call in that block is. This is a test coverage/precision issue rather than a product bug shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java:180 — The new resolveClient fallback (lookup by clientId) is untested; every client permission in the tests passes the internal UUID (myclient.getId()).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `resolveClient(...)` in `AdminPermissionsSchema` with a nontrivial fallback from `getClientById(realm, id)` to `getClientByClientId(realm, id)`. In the new/updated tests, client-specific permissions are created using the internal UUID (e.g., `createPermission(client, myclient.getId(), clientsType, ...)` in `PermissionClientTest`), and no test appears to create a permission/resource using a clientId string (like "myclient") to exercise the fallback path. So the finding about the fallback being untested is accurate and is a specific, diff-grounded test coverage gap rather than a proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/AdminPermissions.java:77 — The new feature gate on the removal listener has no test: nothing deletes a client, role or group that has a per-resource FGAP permission under V2, and nothing checks the V1 cleanup still runs.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `AdminPermissions.registerListener` to only perform cleanup on `RoleRemovedEvent`, `ClientRemovedEvent`, and `GroupRemovedEvent` when `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)` is true (new outer `if` block). The added/modified tests in this PR focus on permission evaluation (e.g., `PermissionClientTest` creating/updating clients, mapping roles) but do not assert that removal events trigger the expected `setPermissionsEnabled(..., false)` cleanup, nor do they cover the new feature-gated behavior (enabled vs disabled) for these listeners. This is a specific test-gap introduced by the new gate, not a directly verifiable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/AbstractPermissionTest.java:136 — The createClientPolicy helper is added but never used, so client-policy-based permissions on the Clients resource type are not covered.

adjudication.rationale: In AbstractPermissionTest a new helper `createClientPolicy(...)` is added (creates a `ClientPolicyRepresentation` and registers cleanup), but in the provided diff there are no call sites using it. The new client permission tests in `PermissionClientTest` grant permissions via `createUserPolicy(...)` only, so client-policy-based permissions for the newly added `Clients` resource type/scopes are not exercised by these tests.
